Hilton's film had a budget of $2 million but only earned about $27,000 at the box office. "Under Obama's new plan, they wouldn't even have to pay taxes," Wilson deadpanned. Myers added worst actor to the "Love Guru" worst picture and worst screenplay Razzies. To save anyone else from having to watch it, Wilson shredded a DVD copy of the film on stage. Parody films "Disaster Movie" and "Meet the Spartans," each nominated in five categories, came away empty-handed. However, that doesn't mean the Razzie foundation thinks they were worthwhile. "When you invest the kind of money that a mainstream, big-budget star film requires, you want some insurance that your investment is going to come back to you. Enter "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull," this year's winner of the worst prequel, remake, rip-off or sequel award. "A fourth installment of a beloved franchise, but this one found itself loved by almost no one," hosts Katsy Chappell and Josh Thoemke said. The approximately 740 voting members of the Raspberry Foundation also found Pierce Brosnan's singing voice sorely lacking. His role in "Mama Mia" earned him the worst supporting actor award. "An actor who could not sing, should not sing and arguably did not sing, in a role he should not have accepted," Razzie hosts Chip Dornell and Kelie McIver said about the former James Bond. But perhaps the biggest "winner" of the night was Uwe Boll. Recipient of the worst director award, the foundation also recognized his lifetime work with the worst career achievement award. Boll is the "worst living director on Earth," Wilson told CNN. Boll had a sense of humor about his Razzie success. He sent in a video rejection speech from a fake set of Darfur, Sudan, saying the Razzies had ruined his life and he would never be back. The Razzie team is already predicting next year's nominees. A few to watch out for: "Hannah Montana," "Friday the 13th" and "Bride Wars," -- the last of which has already grossed more than $50 million. "It's kind of like watching a train wreck, isn't it?" Wilson said.

Mike Myers won worst actor, while “Love Guru” also took worst picture and worst screenplay. In an effort to spare others from seeing it, Wilson destroyed a DVD copy of the movie onstage with a shredder.

The spoof films “Disaster Movie” and “Meet the Spartans,” which were each nominated in five categories, did not win any awards. Still, that did not mean the Razzie Foundation considered them good. The roughly 740 members of the Raspberry Foundation who vote on the awards also judged Pierce Brosnan’s singing harshly. His performance in “Mamma Mia” earned him worst supporting actor. “The Razzies have always had a soft spot for performances that seem to be about fame first and acting second,” Wilson said. “Paris Hilton had the kind of year our voters couldn’t ignore.”

German filmmaker **Uwe Boll**, a frequent target of critics for his video game adaptations and low-budget genre films, received **Worst Director** for a trio of 2008 releases, including **“In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale,” “Postal”** and **“1968 Tunnel Rats.”** Boll also received the Razzies’ **Worst Career Achievement** award.

## Biggest “Winners” of the Night

### Worst Picture  
**Winner: _Space Hamsters 3: Rodents of the Galaxy_**

The animated/live-action hybrid took home the night’s top dishonor after critics described it as “visually aggressive” and “a film that appears to have been rendered during a thunderstorm.”

The movie, a sequel few remembered asking for, followed a team of wisecracking hamsters attempting to save the universe from a black hole made of cheese.

Accepting the award via pre-recorded video, fictional producer **Darren Pike** said:

> “We’re thrilled to receive this recognition. When we set out to make _Space Hamsters 3_, our goal was to entertain children, confuse parents, and sell lunchboxes. Two out of three isn’t bad.”

---

### Worst Actor  
**Winner: Brock Blaze, _Agent Thunder: Tax Day_**

Blaze won for his performance as an elite spy forced to save the world while also filing an extension with the IRS.

Critics singled out his emotional range, which one reviewer described as “somewhere between a refrigerator and a refrigerator wearing sunglasses.”

In his mock acceptance statement, Blaze said:

> “I gave this role everything I had: one facial expression, two leather jackets, and a deep commitment to not blinking.”

---

### Worst Actress  
**Winner: Celeste Moon, _The Duchess of Mars_**

Moon’s turn as a space aristocrat trying to bring etiquette to a collapsing Martian colony earned widespread Razzie attention.

Her character’s signature line — “In space, no one can hear you curtsy” — became an instant meme.

A presenter joked:

> “Celeste didn’t just chew the scenery. She asked for seconds.”

Moon, who did not attend, reportedly sent a note reading:

> “I accept this award in the spirit intended: lightly, reluctantly, and through my agent.”

---

### Worst Supporting Actor  
**Winner: Kip Dalton, _Vampire Lifeguards_**

Dalton played a 600-year-old vampire assigned to patrol a sunny beach, a role that required him to hiss dramatically at both sunlight and teenagers running near the pool.

His performance was praised by Razzie voters for “commitment to a concept nobody explained.”

Dalton accepted in person and said:

> “I’d like to thank the director for believing I could play ancient, mysterious, and allergic to sunscreen. And I’d like to thank the wig department for creating something that looked frightened to be on my head.”

---

### Worst Supporting Actress  
**Winner: Linda Sparks, _Grandma Drift 2_**

Sparks played a retired school principal turned underground street racer in the follow-up to the surprise cult flop _Grandma Drift_.

While audiences enjoyed her commitment, the film’s eight-minute monologue about transmission fluid was less warmly received.

Sparks joked from the stage:

> “People said older women don’t get action roles. I proved them wrong. Then the screenplay proved everyone else right.”

---

## Technical “Achievements” Also Recognized

### Worst Screenplay  
**Winner: _The Algorithm Knows Love_**

A romantic comedy about two dating-app chatbots who fall in love after accidentally matching with each other, _The Algorithm Knows Love_ was criticized for dialogue that sounded “written by a toaster with commitment issues.”

Sample line highlighted during the ceremony:

> “My heart has updated its terms and conditions.”

The screenplay’s fictional writing team issued a statement:

> “We are honored, surprised, and already developing a sequel in which two smart refrigerators navigate divorce.”

---

### Worst Director  
**Winner: Trent Voss, _Moon Cop: Lunar Justice_**

Voss received the award for a film in which a police detective solves crimes on the moon despite there being, according to several critics, “no apparent laws, suspects, gravity, or plot.”

One Razzie voter called it:

> “The first movie where the chase scenes moved slower than the exposition.”

Voss responded with good humor:

> “Directing _Moon Cop_ was a challenge because space is silent, and unfortunately, so were many of the audience reactions.”

---

### Worst Remake, Rip-off, or Sequel  
**Winner: _Pirates of the Cul-de-Sac_**

The family adventure film attempted to transform suburban homeowners’ association drama into a swashbuckling epic.

The plot revolved around a dad who discovers an ancient treasure map hidden in a lawn-care invoice.

Presenter **Nina Vale** quipped:

> “It had everything: pirates, sprinklers, zoning complaints, and a third act that felt like being trapped at a neighborhood meeting.”

---

## Special Razzie Moment: The “Most Unnecessary Franchise Expansion” Award

A new category was introduced this year: **Most Unnecessary Franchise Expansion**, honoring Hollywood’s unstoppable urge to build cinematic universes out of things that may have worked better as one movie, or perhaps no movie.

### Winner: _The Toasterverse Begins_

The film, billed as the launch of a planned seven-part saga centered on sentient kitchen appliances, was widely mocked after its post-credits scene introduced “The Blender Council.”

Host Marcy Lane remarked:

> “Some movies leave you wanting more. _The Toasterverse Begins_ left audiences wanting breakfast and legal representation.”

---

## Audience Reaction

Outside the venue, attendees were divided between irony and genuine affection for the films recognized.

Film blogger **Theo Grant** told CNN:

> “The Razzies serve an important purpose. They remind Hollywood that not every idea needs a multiverse.”

Another attendee, wearing a homemade _Space Hamsters 3_ T-shirt, defended the night’s big winner:

> “Was it bad? Yes. Did I watch it three times? Also yes. Sometimes art is a disaster you invite into your home.”

---

## Predictions for Next Year’s Razzie Nominees

While the night focused on the year’s cinematic misfires, speculation quickly turned to next year’s potential contenders.

Industry watchers say several upcoming projects already have Razzie voters sharpening their pencils.

### Early Predicted Nominees

**_Mall Cop Dracula_**  
A horror-comedy about a vampire security guard protecting a shopping center from werewolf shoplifters. Early buzz suggests the tagline — “He vants to see your receipt” — may be doing a lot of heavy lifting.

**_Fast & Flurrious_**  
A high-speed holiday action film in which street racers must save Christmas by drifting through a blizzard to deliver presents. Analysts predict strong chances in the Worst Pun-Based Title category, should that category ever exist.

**_A.I. President: Oval Office Update_**  
A political thriller about an artificial intelligence elected president after going viral for giving inspirational weather reports. Expected to compete heavily in Worst Screenplay and Most Accidental Social Commentary.

**_Jurassic Parking Lot_**  
A dinosaur disaster movie set entirely outside a shopping mall. According to its fictional studio, the film is “smaller in scale, but bigger in emotional tire damage.”

**_The Gritty Little Mermaid: Reloaded_**  
A dark reboot in which a mermaid trades her voice not for love, but for “revenge, branding rights, and a limited streaming series.”

---

## Closing Remarks

As the ceremony wrapped, Lane reminded the crowd that the Razzies are, at their best, less about cruelty than comic perspective.

> “Bad movies are still movies,” she said. “They employ crews, create memories, and give us something to text about afterward in all caps.”

The night ended with the traditional Razzie group toast: plastic cups raised high, everyone cheering to “better scripts, shorter runtimes, and fewer origin stories for furniture.”

And with that, Hollywood’s least coveted awards signed off for another year — leaving behind a trail of golden spray-painted raspberries, bruised egos, and at least one rumored sequel to _Space Hamsters 3_.

CNN’s fictional entertainment desk will continue monitoring developments, assuming the Blender Council allows it.
